title: The Man from Snowy River
tagline: The ride was hard. The tucker was better.
about: A young man proves himself as a horseman in the Australian high country.
cue: Serve the mains when Jim rides down the mountain after the brumbies.
faces: Serve the mains when Jim rides down the mountain after the brumbies.
“I'll be back for them. And for whatever else is mine.” Jim Craig

    StartersStockman's damperOven-baked damper loaf with butter and golden syrupHow to make it100g butter450g self-raising flour1 pinch salt300ml full cream milkgolden syrup, to serveRub a portion of the butter into the flour and salt.Mix in the milk with a knife, shape into a round and score the top.Bake at 200°C until it sounds hollow.Serve warm with the remaining butter and golden syrup.High country corned beef sandwichesSliced corned silverside with English mustard and pickles on buttered breadHow to make it1.2kg corned silverside1 brown onion1 carrot1 tsp peppercorns8 slices of white bread30g butter2 tbsp English mustard4 tbsp mustard picklesPut the beef in a pot with the halved onion, carrot and peppercorns, cover with water and bring to a simmer.Simmer gently, then leave to cool in the liquid.Butter the bread, slice the beef thin and layer with mustard and pickles.MainsCamp oven lamb stewLamb, carrot, potato and rosemary stew. No wallabyHow to make it1.2kg lamb shoulder chops2 brown onions3 carrots600g potatoes750ml chicken stock1 bunch rosemary1 bunch parsleyChop the onions, carrots and potatoes into chunks.Brown the lamb in a heavy pot in batches.Add the vegetables, stock and rosemary, cover and cook over coals or at 160°C until the lamb is tender.Finish with chopped parsley.Harrison's homestead roastHarrison has no brother.How to make itAs written, serves 4Beef sirloin roasted pink and carved at the table, with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes and pumpkin, horseradish cream and red wine gravy.Season a 1.5kg beef sirloin and roast at 200°C for 40 minutes until 52°C inside, then rest 20 minutes.Roast 800g potatoes and 600g pumpkin in oil at 220°C for 45 minutes.Whisk 140g flour, 3 eggs and 250ml milk, pour into 12 hot oiled muffin holes and bake at 230°C for 20 minutes.Make gravy with the juices, 125ml red wine and 300ml stock.Mix 150g sour cream with horseradish.SweetsSteamed spotted dog currant puddingSteamed currant pudding with golden syrup and custardHow to make it100g butter250g self-raising flour75g caster sugar150g currants150ml full cream milkgolden syrup, to serve600ml custardRub the butter into the flour, then stir in the sugar and currants.Add the milk to make a soft dough and wrap in a floured cloth or put in a basin.Steam until firm and cooked through.Slice and serve with golden syrup and warm custard.DrinksClancy's billy teaLoose leaf tea boiled in a billy, served with milk and sugarHow to make it1.2 L water3 tbsp loose leaf tea200ml full cream milksugar, to tasteBoil the water in a billy or pot.Throw in the tea and a gum leaf if you have one, take it off the heat and swing it round to settle the leaves.Pour into tin mugs with milk and sugar.
